title: Lewandowski et al. finite-strain J2 self-weight beam
purpose: Provide an independent, fail-closed structure-level promotion gate for finite-strain J2 plasticity with finite rotation, distributed loading, membrane stiffening, MPI and restart evidence.
physics: Three-dimensional slender beam under a ramped gravity-like body force, with a left clamp, right-end axial symmetry constraint, finite rotations, isotropic J2 plasticity and linear isotropic hardening.

source.title: Multifield finite strain plasticity: Theory and numerics
source.journal: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 414 (2023), 116101

oracle.identity: The promotion manifest must bind the exact CSV bytes by SHA-256 and attest the pinned upstream commit and both source-artifact digests.

execution.evidence: The candidate driver records an AgentFEM curve but returns incomplete unless a separately executed curve is content-bound to the pinned public MGIS/FEniCS/MFront sources and every observer, convergence, MPI and restart gate is supplied.

observables: Downward displacement versus load factor at the reconciled right-end observer.
Normalized RMS and maximum curve errors against an independently executed reference curve.
acceptance: The reference source commit, solver digest, behaviour digest and CSV content digest must all match their independently archived declarations.
The paper's top-edge point-A wording and the public script's (1, 0, 0) observer must be reconciled explicitly.
Normalized RMS curve error must not exceed 3 percent and normalized maximum error must not exceed 5 percent; these are AgentFEM project contracts, not author-published tolerances.
Candidate mesh and increment convergence, serial/MPI equivalence and checkpoint/restart equivalence are mandatory.
Missing provenance or verification evidence produces incomplete; an available curve outside tolerance produces failed.
limitations: The publication provides a plotted response but no tabulated numerical oracle, and no independently reexecuted curve is bundled; the benchmark is not promoted.
The current environment lacks the legacy FEniCS, MGIS and MFront stack needed to execute the upstream implementation.

AgentFEM uses multiplicative plastic kinematics with quadratic Hencky elasticity and a Kirchhoff-stress J2 return, whereas the public MFront demo uses a total-Hencky formulation; this is a cross-formulation structural comparison rather than bitwise reproduction.
The paper and public script identify different right-end observation locations, so observer reconciliation is a required gate.
The candidate currently uses the expert body-force step because the public affine-periodic model.step route does not accept natural-load power.
references: Lewandowski et al., Multifield finite strain plasticity: Theory and numerics, CMAME 414 (2023) 116101, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cma.2023.116101
